sections.overview: The lowland tapir is a large browsing mammal native to tropical South America.
sections.identification: Its flexible, short trunk helps it grasp leaves and fruit; young tapirs have a striped and spotted coat.
sections.habitat: It uses a range of tropical forest habitats, including terra firme and seasonally flooded forest.
sections.diet: It browses on leaves and fruit, with fruit forming an important part of its diet.
sections.behavior: It is generally solitary and often active at night or around dusk and dawn.
sections.reproduction: After a gestation lasting more than a year, a female usually gives birth to one calf.
sections.ecology: By passing intact seeds in its dung, the tapir helps disperse plants through tropical forests.
sections.conservation: The global IUCN assessment classifies the lowland tapir as Vulnerable; habitat loss and hunting are major pressures.
